cohort: The study analyzed data from 71,744 nonanomalous singletons included in nine Maternal-Fetal Medicine Units Network studies, comparing SGA to AGA newborns.
finding: Small-for-gestational-age (SGA) newborns had a significantly higher likelihood of stillbirth and neonatal mortality compared to appropriate-for-gestational-age (AGA) newborns.
followup_time: up to 28 days after birth (neonatal period)
birth_weight: SGA (birth weight < 10% for estimated gestational age [EGA]) and AGA (birth weight at 10-89% for EGA)
gest_age: 24 weeks or more (with subgroup analyses for 32 weeks or more, and 35 weeks onward)
